Autumn fashion in a complex, connected everyday moment. A reference-guided fashion subject, portrayed as a generated adult woman, is working at a small rooftop theatre rehearsal as an autumn gust lifts the loose corner of a painted canvas backdrop. Her visible face and hair cues follow the supplied image: the same softly tapered facial outline, rounded dark eyes, small straight nose and softly full lips, with a short black bob curving around the jaw and a light, wispy fringe crossing the forehead. Her individual presence comes through attentive concentration and a quiet ease in the cold air. She is wearing autumn layers: a cropped cocoa-and-charcoal tweed jacket with a nubby, flecked weave over a fine cream rib-knit roll-neck, a knee-length checked wool skirt with deep box pleats, and dark chocolate leather knee boots. The knit collar rises above the jacket's turned collar, and its narrow cuffs emerge beyond the tweed sleeves. The cropped jacket hem leaves the skirt waistband and the opening of the first box pleat readable; the checks turn with the folds instead of lying flat across them. Soft creases at the boot ankles register the weight of her stance. These tactile layers remain the strongest visual rhythm after her face and hands. Both boots are planted on dry wooden boards, her left foot half a step forward and knees softly bent, with her shoulders balanced over her feet. A brass ring fixed to a waist-high backstage rail sits on her right side, clear of the jacket front. Her right hand grips the doubled canvas seam just beyond the ring and draws the corner through it; her left hand holds the folded edge against the near side of the ring, keeping the loop from slipping back. Each forearm leads visibly from its own sleeve to its hand. The gathered corner now hangs as a compact vertical tail beneath the ring, while the free upper canvas still bows in the wind. Its painted blue arch is kinked by the pulled fold, making the change in tension visible. Her gaze rests on the attachment, her lips gently parted as the next knot waits to be made. A chalk stage mark and two folded rehearsal chairs situate this brief repair within the rehearsal space. Photograph the moment from a front three-quarter position at her waist height, in a vertical 4:5 full-length environmental frame with her face, both hands, the ring, skirt folds and boots visible together. Place the moving canvas toward the right edge and leave breathing space around the attachment. Cool late-afternoon skylight reveals the tweed and wool surfaces; a warm rehearsal lamp by the open theatre door gives a small amber edge to her cheek and knit collar. Keep natural skin texture, believable fabric weight and moderate depth of field, with the subject and contact plane crisp and the distant roof parapet softly receding.

definitions.principle: These creative definitions guide agent-owned choices within requester meaning, not clinical classifications. Zero/off disables added treatment, never removes explicitly requested content or artistic judgment. Expression levels describe prominence in the whole image; creativity levels describe interpretive freedom. Neither measures exposure percentages, detail quotas, quality scores, or native image-model parameters. Intensity and expression are separate choices; higher intensity does not prescribe a garment, material or expression category. Creativity leaves style, extra props and surreal treatment open to the request and artistic judgment. Emphasis directs only active sensual and fetish axes without changing their intensities. Popular permits familiar appeal without requiring trend search; overt is an available expression, not the mandatory meaning of level three. Choose a coherent expression suited to this particular scene. Sensual and fetish may share the same expressive choice.
